notes:
Feature release for the agent generation channel: an explicit, operator-written declared upstream served model (declaredServedModel) on each AI provider configuration.

Why: the P4 production acceptance run (desc5 r3) reached generation over the LAN relay at http://host.docker.internal:8317/v1 (cli-proxy-api) and the call itself succeeded (HTTP 200 in 79 s), but the generator refused with served_model_mismatch. The relay accepts gemini-3.8-flash-high and reports gemini-3.8-flash-n in the response, while it rejects gemini-3.8-flash-n and gemini-3.8-flash as request names (model_not_found). No platform-side model name can make the requested and reported names equal.

What changes: the generation guard keeps its meaning (a reported model that differs from the configured model is refused) with exactly one exception, a name the operator wrote into the AI settings as the declared served model. A third name is still refused, the existing test that forbids a hardcoded response-model exception still passes, and every accepted generation records requestedModel, servedModel and declaredServedModel in its provenance. An empty field behaves exactly like v0.2.25.

Behaviour change at save time: testAiProviderConnection now returns the model name reported by the probe response, and saving an AI configuration compares it on the spot. The configured name or the declared name passes; any other name is refused with a message naming both. When the probe response carries no model name nothing is concluded either way. Consequence: re-saving a configuration that points at a renaming relay without a declaration now fails when saving instead of at the first generation. The Test connection and Validate model buttons now report the upstream name and whether it matches the configuration or the declaration. Stored configurations are not re-validated on read, so the production organization keeps generating refusals until the declaration is saved.

Database: no migrations. The schema stays at 050 as applied by v0.2.24, so an upgrade from v0.2.25 does not need the worker/dispatcher stop that a migration-bearing upgrade requires.

Rollback target: v0.2.25 application images only. The new field lives inside the encrypted service-settings JSON, which is read without a strict schema; v0.2.25 ignores it, so generations through a renaming relay are refused again (the safe direction) and a re-save under v0.2.25 drops the field. No persisted record shape outside that JSON changes.

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.24/v0.2.25, so an installation already on v0.2.25 upgrades with the updater it has. Explicit rollback requires the exact rollbackCompatibleFrom array member.

Validation before tagging, on a clean worktree of commit 94b6487 (this release commit adds only this manifest file): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm --filter api test 2098 passed / 181 skipped / 0 failed (the main working tree shows 48 more, all of them another session's uncommitted WordPress tests that this release does not contain); pnpm typecheck with zero errors; pnpm build; the BFF routing verification 124/124 across the ip, domain and tunnel Caddy templates (real Caddy v2.10.2 -> built Next BFF -> synthetic API); the CI static entry-point and bootstrap-contract checks including the 23 Python retention cases. Browser verification of both AI settings forms passed (scripts/verify-ai-declared-served-model-ui.mjs). CI re-runs the full suite and the image checks.

Not asserted here: the P4 production acceptance itself. After deployment the declaration still has to be saved for the production organization and the acceptance re-run.
